description: Hi there, my name is Josiah. I'm 4 years old and fascinated with planets and everything space related. This is Little Explorers Big Universe! My mum, dad and I are travelling to Mars to investigate all of the equipment we've found. Together we'll be building an illustrated picture/fact/activity story for children to learn with. We would love to work with others with an interest in Science/Arts/Technology.🌕 🌑 ☄️ 🌌👨‍👩‍👦🔴🛰️
summary:
The Forgotten Explorers is an interactive read-along picture book for ages 3 to 7,
addressing the prompt "Abandoned but not Forgotten". It describes the many spacecraft and probes that remain on the Moon, on Mars and further out in the Solar System, prompted by a child and answered by a parent using NASA information. In 41 pages, it covers the Apollo 11 LM descent module, LRVs, ALSEP, Surveyor series, Viking 1 & 2, Sojourner, Spirit & Opportunity, Phoenix, InSight, Ingenuity, Pioneer 10 & 11, Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker and Kepler. The function and findings of each are described, and it follows how information is relayed to the scientists studying them here on Earth. By describing these abandoned craft to young children, it provides a broader insight into the NASA programme and encourages them to question what comes next.
details:
The Forgotten Explorers is an animated interactive picture book for 3-7 year olds. It tells the story of the spacecraft and equipment we've left on the Moon, Mars and out in space. Over the course of 41 brief pages, our explorer asks a question, and "Mom" provides the factual answer based on information from NASA.
There is some animation throughout the book, including planets orbiting/rotating, rovers driving, Ingenuity's rotors turning, moonquakes & marsquakes, and a Mars dust storm. The child can tap the screen to reveal Mom's answer, or tap the "Read to me" button to have the page read out to them. On the "Meet the Planets" page, they can tap each planet in its orbit to hear its name and discover where Mars is. Compatible with any internet browser (desktop/tablet/phone), it can be navigated with arrow buttons and/or swiping. A PDF copy is provided to print.
We wanted to make it accessible for younger children, particularly with ADHD but with an interest in the planets. With brief page lengths, animations and interactivity, the child is encouraged to keep going, with a progress bar at the bottom of the page. A "Calm" button will remove animations for children that find it overstimulating.
Astronomical equipment covered includes: Apollo 11 LM (Eagle), 3x LRVs, ALSEPs, Surveyors, Viking 1 & 2, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, InSight, Ingenuity, Pioneer 10 & 11, Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker and Kepler. Each is given a brief description of its purpose and findings.
It started with a question from our son (age 4) "Why is Mars red?", which then snowballed into the idea of this book. He has included some of his artwork of outer space and his Explorer is dressed in his handcrafted Explorer suit made by his mother. It closes with a prompt for the child to ask the next question.
Children are often only introduced to current, ongoing space exploration. This allows them to learn about some that are no longer operating and how we can continue to learn from them. And that they can explore too!
